cleanIntro: The RAD 9 and the RAD 45 come apart by design, and HUXWRX covers both in one book. Each ships in its long configuration: a serialized titanium Housing, a Housing Module, a stack of interchangeable Flow-Baffles and a Cap, with a Booster Assembly (Piston, Spring, Piston Base and O-ring) at the rear. The two differ in the Piston: ½-28 on the RAD 9, .578-28 on the RAD 45. HUXWRX's book sets two cycles: the booster greased and its O-ring checked before every session, and the housing and baffles taken down every 1,000 rounds or less. The included RAD 9 & 45 Wrench does every removal and every torque in this guide.

steps.title: Clear the host before the can is touched
steps.action: Unload the host firearm before either end of the can is handled: magazine out, every round off the bench, and the chamber checked by eye and by finger. HUXWRX prints that order at the head of both its installation and its cleaning sections, so it applies whether the can is coming off or going on. The host's own manual is the authority on how its action is cleared.
steps.prose: Every removal on this can is wrench work directly in front of the muzzle. A chamber you only looked at is not a chamber you checked.
steps.quote: WARNING: Ensure the firearm is unloaded. Remove the magazine and all ammunition from the workspace. Visually and physically check that the chamber is clear.
steps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR INSTALLATION, p.2
steps.warn: Look and feel: the chamber is checked both ways.

steps.title: Let it cool before you handle it
steps.action: After firing, the suppressor can be hot enough to burn skin and clothing. Give it time to cool, or handle it in heat-resistant gloves, before a hand or the wrench goes near the Piston flats. Set it down where it cannot burn anything while it cools.
steps.prose: HUXWRX puts this on the first page of the book, ahead of any procedure.
steps.quote: The suppressor system can reach extremely hot temperatures. Use caution before handling after use. Avoid contact with skin or clothing when hot.
steps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — WARNING, p.1
steps.warn: Hot cans burn. Wait, or wear gloves.

steps.title: The right ammunition, and a barrel thread that matches your Piston
steps.action: HUXWRX's book does not print a cartridge rating for either can. What it requires is a serviceable host and ammunition of the correct caliber, and what it states about the mount is that the RAD 9 comes with a ½-28 Piston and the RAD 45 with a .578-28 Piston. So the host barrel must carry your can's thread, and the book's own installation check is that the barrel and accessory thread pattern match. If you are not certain of your can's rating, ask HUXWRX before you fire it.
steps.prose: Know which of the two cans you have before it goes on a gun: the two Pistons are different threads.
steps.quote: Only operate the suppressor system with a serviceable firearm and ammunition of the correct caliber.
steps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — WARNING, p.1
steps.warn: Thread pattern and caliber both match the host, or it does not go on.

steps.title: Booster on a recoiling barrel; spacer or adapter only on a fixed one
steps.action: Both cans ship with the Booster Assembly fitted, and the booster's Spring is what lets the can work on a host whose barrel moves to cycle, such as a tilting-barrel pistol. HUXWRX's alternatives, the Fixed Barrel Spacer in place of the Spring or the Direct Thread Adapter on its own, are only for hosts whose barrel is fixed and does not move. Know which one is in your can before it goes on a gun.
steps.prose: The Direct Thread Adapter goes on by itself: the book has every accessory part removed first.
steps.quote: The Booster Assembly with Spring is necessary to function on weapon systems where the barrel reciprocates to cycle.
steps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ACCESSORY INSTALLATION, item 1, p.2
steps.warn: The Fixed Barrel Spacer and the Direct Thread Adapter are for a barrel that does not reciprocate.

steps.title: Off the host with the wrench on the Piston flats
steps.action: If the host is a handgun, lock the slide back first. Then put the included RAD 9 & 45 Wrench, with a torque wrench or an adjustable wrench, on the Piston's wrench flats and unscrew the suppressor from the barrel. It was tightened on at up to 125 lbf-in, so expect it to need the tool rather than a hand on the tube.
steps.prose: The open slide is there for room: HUXWRX has you lock it open so the wrench and torque wrench clear the frame.
steps.quote: To detach the suppressor from the host firearm (lock the slide back if a handgun) use the RAD 9 & 45 Wrench and torque wrench or adjustable wrench on the Piston wrench
steps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, Booster and Fixed Barrel Assembly, p.2
steps.warn: The tool goes on the Piston flats.

steps.title: Booster Assembly out of the Housing
steps.action: Hold the Piston Base flats with the RAD 9 & 45 Wrench and, if it needs an opposing force, put an adjustable wrench on the Piston flats, then unscrew the Booster Assembly from the Housing. The book's every-session care is for this assembly, the grease on the Piston, Spring and O-ring and the check of the O-ring inside the Piston Base, and this is its instruction for getting it off the Housing. Stop at the booster: the Cap, the Housing Module and the Flow-Baffles stay put until the Deep Clean.
steps.prose: The book also says the serialized Housing contains a stainless Piston Base fitted at the factory with high temp thread locker, and it gives no instruction to remove that. If what you are turning will not break free with the wrench where the book puts it, stop and contact HUXWRX rather than adding force.
steps.quote: To disassemble the Booster and Fixed Barrel Assemblies from the Housing, use the RAD 9 & 45 Wrench on the Piston Base flats along with an adjustable wrench on the Piston flats if necessary.
steps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ACCESSORY INSTALLATION, item 4, p.2
steps.warn: Wrench on the flats the book names. No extra force on a joint that will not break.

steps.title: Grease the Piston, Spring and O-ring
steps.action: Before every session, put a light coat of high-temperature grease on the bearing surfaces of the Piston, the Spring and the O-ring. HUXWRX ships the booster greased and repeats this instruction in two places in its book, so it belongs to every range trip, not to the Deep Clean. The booster is what lets a recoiling-barrel pistol cycle with the can on, so it is the part that gets attention every time.
steps.prose: High temperature grease, as the book specifies, and a light coat.
steps.quote: Recommended maintenance cycle for the Booster Assembly is to, before each session, apply a light coat of high temperature grease on the bearing surfaces of the Piston, Spring, and O-ring.
steps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, Booster and Fixed Barrel Assembly, p.2

steps.title: Check the O-ring inside the Piston Base
steps.action: Look at the O-ring on the inside of the Piston Base for damage before each session. A damaged O-ring comes out and is replaced with a 018 size Viton O-ring, which HUXWRX supplies. Replacing it is part of normal booster care.
steps.prose: The size is printed in the book: 018, Viton.
steps.quote: Inspect the O-ring on the inside of the Piston Base for damage before each session. If damaged, remove and replace it with a 018 size Viton O-ring available through HUXWRX.
steps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, Booster and Fixed Barrel Assembly, p.2

steps.title: Clean the Piston, then every thread
steps.action: The Pistons are heat-treated, nitride-coated stainless steel, and HUXWRX's methods for them are CLP with a brass or nylon brush, or an ultrasonic cleaner. Then clean every thread you are about to put back together: the barrel's, the Piston's, the Piston Base's and the Housing's. The book asks for clean threads before every assembly it describes.
steps.prose: Clean threads are what let the can seat and torque as the book intends.
steps.quote: The Pistons and Direct Thread Adapters are heat treated and nitride coated stainless steel. They can be cleaned with CLP and a brass or nylon brush and or in an ultrasonic cleaner.
steps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, Housing and Flow-Baffles, p.2

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The can is off the host and the Booster Assembly is out of the Housing. The Cap, the Housing Module and the Flow-Baffles stay on the Housing for this clean: HUXWRX's cycle for the housing and baffles is every 1,000 rounds or less. Next comes the booster's every-session care and clean threads.
steps.prose: Reassembly for this path is the booster back in and the can back on the host.
steps.quote: Disassemble the assembly down to the individual components shown in the exploded assembly view.
steps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, Housing and Flow-Baffles, p.2

deepSteps.title: Cap and Housing Module off the Housing
deepSteps.action: With the can off the host and the booster out, unscrew the Cap and Housing Module from the Housing using the included RAD 9 & 45 Wrench or an adjustable wrench. The Cap was torqued to 100 lbf-in, so expect a firm break. HUXWRX's note is that an adjustable wrench on the piston flats can be used as the opposing force.
deepSteps.prose: This is the same operation the book uses to change the can's length, so the parts it frees are the ones it expects you to handle.
deepSteps.quote: Unscrew the Cap and Housing Module from the Housing using the included RAD 9 & 45 Wrench or adjustable wrench.
deepSteps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — RAD 9 & 45 ASSEMBLY AND INSTALLATION, length configuration item 1, p.2

deepSteps.title: Push the Flow-Baffles out with a dowel
deepSteps.action: HUXWRX notes that the Flow-Baffles protrude from the end of the housing. Push them out with a 1/2 or 5/8 inch dowel, the two sizes the book names. Wear safety glasses and chemical resistant gloves from here on, as the cleaning warning asks.
deepSteps.prose: The book names the dowel and its two sizes; nothing else is called for here.
deepSteps.quote: A 1/2” or 5/8” dowel can be used to push out the Flow-Baffles.
deepSteps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — HOUSING, p.1

deepSteps.title: Separate the Flow-Baffles
deepSteps.action: If the Flow-Baffles hold together, separate them with a flat head screwdriver, the tool the book names. They are interchangeable and do not need to be timed to each other, so you need not track which one came from where. They do go back seated together in the order the book's figure shows.
deepSteps.prose: Interchangeable is HUXWRX's word. It is what makes this can quick to put back.
deepSteps.quote: A flat head screwdriver can be used to separate the Flow-Baffles.
deepSteps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — HOUSING, p.1

deepSteps.title: This is as far as it comes apart
deepSteps.action: Stop at the components the book's exploded views show: the Housing, the Housing Module, the Flow-Baffles and the Cap, and the booster's Piston, Spring, Piston Base and O-ring. HUXWRX's warning page forbids disassembling the system beyond the level the manual shows for standard maintenance. The stainless Piston Base the book says is fitted inside the Housing at the factory with high temp thread locker is cleaned in place.
deepSteps.prose: Anything past the exploded view is a question for HUXWRX, not for the bench.
deepSteps.quote: Do not disassemble the suppressor system beyond required level, as shown in this manual, for standard maintenance.
deepSteps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — WARNING, p.1

deepSteps.title: Stainless parts: the book allows the hard methods
deepSteps.action: The Flow-Baffles, the Spring and the Fixed Barrel Spacer are heat-treated stainless steel, and HUXWRX lets you be aggressive with them: a steel bristle brush, a wire wheel, an ultrasonic cleaner, a media tumbler, or hand tools with elbow grease and CLP. Those methods are listed for these stainless parts; the aluminium parts get their own, gentler list below.
deepSteps.prose: Clean in a ventilated place and wash your hands after: the book warns that cleaning firearms exposes you to lead.
deepSteps.quote: Spring, and Fixed Barrel Spacer are heat-treated stainless steel so can be cleaned with a steel bristle brush, wire wheel, ultrasonic cleaner, media tumbler, tools with elbow grease and CLP to remove fouling.
deepSteps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, Housing and Flow-Baffles, p.2

deepSteps.title: The serialized Housing
deepSteps.action: The Housing is titanium with high temp Cerakote. Clean it with CLP, nylon brushes and or an ultrasonic cleaner. A steel bristle brush and tools are for inside the Piston Base, where fouling builds on the Piston interface. Get every thread clean before it goes back together.
deepSteps.prose: The book cleans the factory-fitted stainless Piston Base in place and gives no instruction to remove it.
deepSteps.quote: A steel bristle brush and tools can be used inside the Piston Base to remove fouling from the Piston interface. The Housing can be cleaned with CLP, nylon brushes and or an ultrasonic cleaner. Ensure all threads are clean before reassembly.
deepSteps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, Housing and Flow-Baffles, p.2

deepSteps.title: Aluminium parts: nylon brushes and CLP
deepSteps.action: The Housing Module, the Piston Base and the Cap are hard coat anodized aluminum, and the Housing Module is Cerakoted as well. For these the book names nylon brushes and CLP. The steel brush, wire wheel and tumbler are on the stainless parts' list, not this one.
deepSteps.prose: Get the threads clean on all three before reassembly, as the book asks.
deepSteps.quote: The Housing Module, Piston Base, Cap are hard coat anodized aluminum. The Housing Module is also high temp Cerakoted. Use nylon brushes and CLP to remove any fouling.
deepSteps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, Housing and Flow-Baffles, p.2

deepSteps.title: Flow-Baffles back, seated in the order shown
deepSteps.action: With the threads clean, put the Flow-Baffles back seated together in the order the book's figure shows. They do not need timing relative to each other and they are interchangeable, so seat them fully; there is nothing to index.
deepSteps.prose: The book's figure is the reference for the order.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure all Flow-Baffles are properly seated together in the order shown, they do not need to be timed relative to each other and they are interchangeable.
deepSteps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — RAD 9 & 45 ASSEMBLY AND INSTALLATION, length configuration item 3, p.2

deepSteps.title: Housing Module finger tight, then the Cap to 100 lbf-in
deepSteps.action: For the long configuration the can shipped in, assemble the Housing Module finger tight, then put the Cap on and torque it. Tighten the Cap with the included RAD 9 & 45 Wrench, firmly by hand or with a ¼-inch drive torque wrench to 100 lbf-in (115 kgf-cm). In the short configuration the Cap screws straight into the Housing and takes the same torque.
deepSteps.prose: HUXWRX notes the Cap can be torqued before or after the can is torqued onto a barrel.
deepSteps.quote: When converting back into the long configuration, assemble the Housing Module finger tight then torque the Cap.
deepSteps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — RAD 9 & 45 ASSEMBLY AND INSTALLATION, length configuration item 6, p.2

deepSteps.title: Booster back in: Piston Base to 100 lbf-in
deepSteps.action: Grease the Piston, Spring and O-ring with high-temperature grease and refit the Booster Assembly to the Housing. Tighten the Piston Base with the included RAD 9 & 45 Wrench, firmly by hand or with a ¼-inch drive torque wrench to 100 lbf-in (115 kgf-cm).
deepSteps.prose: The Cap and the Piston Base both have to be firmly tightened or torqued before the can is fired.
deepSteps.quote: Tighten the Piston Base or Direct Thread Adapter using the included RAD 9 & 45 Wrench, firmly by hand or using a ¼ drive torque wrench to 100 lbf-in (115 kgf-cm).
deepSteps.cite: RAD™ 9 & RAD™ 45 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — ACCESSORY INSTALLATION, item 6, p.2

cleaning.name: BOOSTER ASSEMBLY — EVERY SESSION
tasks: A light coat of high-temperature grease on the bearing surfaces of the Piston, Spring and O-ring
The O-ring inside the Piston Base checked for damage; a damaged one is replaced with a 018 size Viton O-ring from HUXWRX
Booster with its Spring on a recoiling-barrel host; the Fixed Barrel Spacer or the Direct Thread Adapter only on a fixed barrel

cleaning.name: PISTON & THREADS
tasks: Piston: CLP with a brass or nylon brush, or an ultrasonic cleaner
Every thread clean before assembly: barrel, Piston, Piston Base, Housing, Housing Module and Cap

cleaning.name: HOUSING & FLOW-BAFFLES — EVERY 1,000 ROUNDS OR LESS
tasks: This group is the Deep Clean: the Cap, Housing Module and Flow-Baffles come out
Flow-Baffles, Spring and Fixed Barrel Spacer (stainless): steel bristle brush, wire wheel, ultrasonic cleaner, media tumbler, or hand tools and CLP
Housing (titanium, Cerakote): CLP, nylon brushes or an ultrasonic cleaner; a steel bristle brush inside the Piston Base for the Piston interface
Housing Module, Piston Base and Cap (anodized aluminum): nylon brushes and CLP
Do not disassemble past the parts the book's exploded views show

cleaning.name: WHILE YOU CLEAN
tasks: Safety glasses and chemical resistant gloves
Adequate ventilation, and hands washed afterwards: cleaning exposes you to lead

reassembly: Clean every thread before assembly: Housing, Housing Module, Cap, Piston Base, Piston and the host barrel.
Seat the Flow-Baffles together in the order the book's figure shows; they need no timing to each other and are interchangeable.
Long configuration: assemble the Housing Module finger tight, then fit the Cap. Short configuration: screw the Cap straight into the Housing.
Tighten the Cap with the included RAD 9 & 45 Wrench, firmly by hand or with a ¼-inch drive torque wrench to 100 lbf-in (115 kgf-cm).
Grease the Piston, Spring and O-ring with high-temperature grease, refit the Booster Assembly, and tighten the Piston Base firmly by hand or to 100 lbf-in (115 kgf-cm).

Handgun host: lock the slide open. Check the barrel and the Piston share a thread pattern, thread the can on until it bottoms out on the crown or shoulder, and tighten the Piston to the barrel with the wrench, firmly by hand or to 125 lbf-in (144 kgf-cm).
fncheck: Before the first shot, confirm the Cap and the Piston Base are both firmly tightened or torqued, which HUXWRX requires before firing, and that the can bottomed out on the barrel's crown or shoulder and was tightened on the Piston flats. On a recoiling-barrel pistol the Booster Assembly with its Spring must be the mount fitted; the Fixed Barrel Spacer and the Direct Thread Adapter are for fixed barrels only.
